head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: Root config sets no-explicit-any and the type-import and unused-vars rules.
The SPA config sets the same no-explicit-any, type-import, unused-vars and no-console rules.

title: The backend ESLint rule block repeats the SPA config's block
body: The no-explicit-any, consistent-type-imports, no-unused-vars (with the same underscore ignore patterns) and no-console rules are written out in full in the root config. The SPA config repeats them. A change to one set of rules has to be remembered in the other, and they can drift apart.
recommendation: Move the shared rule set into one module that both flat configs import. Keep only the boundary-specific rules in each config.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: The refresh condition is keys === null || keys.size === 0 || age >= ttlMs, and age is measured from fetchedAt.
On failure with a usable stale set, nothing is updated, so the next call fetches again.

title: During a JWKS outage every verification re-attempts the network fetch until the stale window ends. (raised by the question sets behaviour and contracts)
body: When a refresh fails but the old key set is still within maxStaleMs, getKey serves the old keys and does not update fetchedAt. The age therefore stays at or above ttlMs, and every later call to getKey runs refresh() again. Calls that overlap share one request, but calls that do not overlap each start a new fetch that can wait up to the 5 s timeout. For up to an hour of outage, each authenticated request can be delayed by that timeout and adds load to the failing Auth endpoint. The header comment says a short outage should not reject valid sessions, but it does not say that requests slow down.
recommendation: Record the time of the last failed attempt and skip refetching for a short backoff while the stale set is still usable.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

recommendation: Export the shared rule set from one module and spread it into both configs, or accept the copy as the deliberate cost of the separate workspace lint.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: home defaults to '/signin' when the registry has no nav items

title: With no registered nav items, '/' redirects to '/signin', and a signed-in user is bounced back to '/' in a loop
body: `home` falls back to '/signin' when `navItemsFor(modules)` is empty. The '/' route redirects to `home`. SignInPage sends a signed-in user to '/' (or `from`). With zero modules, a signed-in user therefore loops between '/' and '/signin'. The six shipped features make this unreachable today, but the fallback is not safe.
recommendation: Fall back to a route that renders in the shell (the not-found page), or fail loudly when no destination is registered.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: setPending(false) runs unconditionally in finally

title: useApiMutation `pending` clears when the first of two overlapping mutations finishes
body: `pending` is a single boolean. If `mutate` is called twice before the first call settles, the first call's `finally` sets pending=false while the second is still in flight. The submit button is re-enabled early, and a late failure of the first call can overwrite `error` and `data` from the second.
recommendation: Count in-flight calls, or ignore results from calls that are no longer the latest.

evidence.shows: literal English title in the ApiError fallback
second copy with another literal English title

title: Hand-written English fallback titles for ApiError bypass t()
body: toApiError in hooks.ts builds an ApiError whose title is the hard-coded string 'The request failed.', or the raw Error.message. screenStatus.ts does the same with 'The screen could not be loaded.'. The title is shown to the user, for example in the ConfirmActionDialog banner and the error states. The rule says every UI string goes through t(). The same mapping is also written twice.
recommendation: Use t() keys for the fallback titles and share one toApiError helper between hooks.ts and screenStatus.ts.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: reasonText state lives in the always-mounted component
acknowledged state lives in the always-mounted component
the reset happens only in close(), which the cancel path uses

title: Reason text and acknowledgement tick survive a confirmed action and are pre-filled the next time the dialog opens
body: The component stays mounted when `open` goes false. Only `close()` resets `reasonText` and `acknowledged`, and the confirm button calls `onConfirm` directly. After a successful confirm, the parent closes the dialog by setting `open` to false. The next open then shows the previous reason, and an `acknowledgement` checkbox that is already ticked. This defeats the gate meant for irrevocable actions.
recommendation: Reset `reasonText` and `acknowledged` whenever `open` becomes false, or after `onConfirm` resolves. Alternatively, key the inner state on `open`.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: reasonText state lives in the always-mounted component
acknowledged state lives in the always-mounted component
the reset runs only inside close()

title: Reason text and acknowledgement are cleared only by the dialog's own close(), not when `open` goes false
body: The component stays mounted when `open` is false (Dialog returns null). The state is reset only inside close(). If a parent closes the dialog after a successful onConfirm by setting open=false, as the pending/error props suggest, the previous reason stays filled and the acknowledgement stays ticked. The next open then shows the old reason, and an irreversible-action acknowledgement is already satisfied, so the confirm button is not blocked. No caller is shown in the package, so this depends on how callers close it.
recommendation: Reset reasonText and acknowledged when `open` becomes false, or key the inner form on each open.

the same nextTheme derivation, followed by the same label, icon and dispatch

title: Theme toggle logic is written twice, in Topbar and UserCard
body: Topbar and UserCard each read the theme, derive nextTheme, pick the dark/light label and icon, and dispatch chooseTheme(nextTheme). A change to the toggle (label key, icon or persistence) must be made in both places or the two controls will drift apart.
recommendation: Extract a small shared hook (for example useThemeToggle returning nextTheme, label, icon and toggle) into the shell folder or app/hooks, and use it in both components.

evidence.shows: the hint paragraph in FieldShell; the error paragraph follows it

title: The hint and error paragraph block is copied into five fields instead of being shared
body: FieldShell renders the hint and error paragraphs with ids `${id}-hint` and `${id}-error`. MultiSelect, Checkbox, RadioGroup and DateTimeInput repeat the same JSX by hand. The ids are what describedBy() points at, so a change in one copy can silently break the aria-describedby linkage of the others.
recommendation: Extract a FieldMessages component (hint, error, id) and use it in FieldShell and in the four other fields.

title: The comment's example is left over from TenderIQ
body: The example, 'Sealed until the opening session', describes a tender-opening concept. ClaimsIQ has no sealed opening session, so the comment misleads the reader about what a restricted state is for in this product.
recommendation: Use a claims-domain example (for example 'Finance figures are not shown to this persona') or delete the example.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: from is computed from page without clamping to pageCount
to is min(total, page*pageSize), so it can be below from

title: Out-of-range page produces an inverted "Showing" range
body: With page=5, pageSize=25, total=50, `from` is 101 and `to` is min(50,125)=50, so the text reads "Showing 101–50 of 50". Nothing in the component clamps `page` to `pageCount`, so any caller that leaves a stale page after the total shrinks (a filter change, for example) shows this.
recommendation: Clamp `page` to `pageCount` before computing `from` and `to`.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: inShell requires slots.title !== null
the page-local h1 is rendered whenever inShell is false

title: Before the shell's title slot is set, PageHeader renders a second h1 in the page
body: AppShell's `titleSlot` starts as null and is set by a callback ref, so on the first render `slots.title` is null. `inShell` is then false, and PageHeader renders `<h1 className="ciq-topbar-title">` in the page head. After the state update the page h1 is removed and the title is portalled into the top bar. Each page mount in a freshly mounted shell shows a transient duplicate h1 and a layout shift.
recommendation: Treat a provided slots context with a null title as in-shell and render nothing until the slot exists, or keep the slot element mounted.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: link onClick only sets open to false and does not restore focus
Escape closes with close(true), which returns focus to the trigger

title: Choosing a link entry closes the menu without returning focus
body: The link entry's onClick only calls setOpen(false). The focused menuitem link is then unmounted, so focus falls to <body> unless the navigation lands somewhere that takes it. Action entries go through close(true) and return focus to the trigger. The design system's own Dialog and focusReturn modules guard against this kind of focus drop, so link entries are treated differently from action entries. No current caller passes a link entry (UserCard uses only text, action and separator entries), so it only shows up once one does.
recommendation: Use close(false) plus a focus move to the main region (MAIN_REGION_ID) for link entries, or call close(true) so focus returns to the trigger.

evidence.shows: The header says VerticalTabs is the settings sub-navigation of `settings.png`.

title: Header comment cites a settings.png mockup that is not part of this repo
body: The VerticalTabs line says it is "the settings sub-navigation of `settings.png`". ClaimsIQ has six placeholder pages and no settings page, and the package contains no such image. The comment points at an artefact the reader cannot find and carries nothing the code needs.
recommendation: Delete the `settings.png` reference. Describe VerticalTabs as a vertical link-tab navigation beside page content, or drop the sentence.

evidence.shows: The initialsOf comment says `Kagiso Dube` → `TM`.
The formatTimeRemaining comment promises `closed 2 days ago`.
The abbreviation regex rejects any GMT-style short name.
The test expects `passed 2 d 0 h ago`, not the commented wording.

title: Doc comments describe behaviour the code does not have
body: The comment on `initialsOf` gives the example `Kagiso Dube` → `TM`, but the function returns `KD`, which the test confirms. The comment on `formatTimeRemaining` promises `closed 2 days ago` and `2 days 4 hours left`. The code produces `passed 2 d 0 h ago` and `2 d 4 h left`. The module comment says an abbreviation like `CAT` is returned, but Intl's en-US short name for Africa/Gaborone is `GMT+2`, which the regex rejects. So `abbreviation` is null for the product's own zone.
recommendation: Correct the comments to match the output, and drop the CAT claim or derive the abbreviation another way.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: The loop breaks on `value < 1024` before the value is rounded.
Values of 100 or more are rounded with `Math.round`, which can give 1024.
`Math.max(minutes, delta >= 0 ? 1 : 0)` forces `1 min` at zero and allows `0 min` in the past.

title: formatBytes shows 1024 KB near a unit boundary, and formatTimeRemaining gives odd output at zero (raised by the question sets behaviour and contracts and repeats)
body: For 1048575 bytes, `value` is 1023.999, which is below 1024, so the loop stops at `kb`. Then `Math.round` gives `1024`, so the result is `1024 KB` instead of `1 MB`. In `formatTimeRemaining`, a delta of exactly 0 or a few seconds ahead renders `1 min left`. A deadline passed by under a minute renders `passed 0 min ago`.
recommendation: Round first and then choose the unit. Give sub-minute deltas their own wording, such as `now`.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: restore is obtained from configureApiClient and only returned to the caller
the afterEach cleans the DOM, storage and theme but does not restore the API client adapters

title: renderWithProviders installs API client adapters and never restores them
body: configureApiClient swaps in module-level adapters whose getTenantId reads this render's store. The restore function is only returned. setup.ts's afterEach does not call it, so the adapters stay installed after each test and leak into later tests in the same file. A test that does not render through this helper but calls the API client sees a stale store and a stale token.
recommendation: Track the restore function inside the helper and call it from an afterEach, or register the cleanup in setup.ts.

evidence.shows: the inShell branch returns ciq-page + PageHeader + body
the standalone branch returns main.ciq-auth-page + PageHeader + ciq-auth-card--wide

title: The in-shell versus standalone page wrapper is written twice
body: NotFoundPage and RouteErrorPage each end with the same branch. In the shell they render `.ciq-page` with a PageHeader and the body card. Outside the shell they render `<main className="ciq-auth-page">` with a PageHeader and `.ciq-auth-card--wide` around the body. A change to one layout (the heading or the class names) has to be copied into the other.
recommendation: Extract one shared wrapper, for example `StatusPageFrame({ inShell, title, children })`, in `pages/`. Both pages would render their card through it.

body: The comment lists `2 days 4 hours left` and `closed 2 days ago`. The catalog templates produce `2 d 4 h left` and `passed 2 d 0 h ago`, and the test expects those strings.

head: 386652682ab8d62e332c81b38bc83ec61342d34a

evidence.shows: the normalisation of the whole stylesheet sits inside rule(), so it is repeated per call
css is read once in beforeAll, so the normalised text could be derived there

title: rule() strips comments and normalises the whole 2379-line stylesheet on every call
body: Each rule() call runs two regex replaces over the full CSS text and then a matchAll over all of it. The tests call it about 15 times, and the stylesheet will keep growing as more contract tests are added. The normalisation depends only on `css`, which is fixed once beforeAll has read the file, so it could be computed once.
recommendation: Compute the comment-stripped, whitespace-normalised text once (in beforeAll or a lazy const) and have rule() only run the matchAll over it.

body:
The test name promises focus returns to the opener, to the main region, or to the given target. The Harness creates a `result` ref (a focusable
